record.original_question: A topological space X is weakly perfect if, for each closed subset C of X, there is a G_delta subset D of X such that D is contained in C and C is the closure of D in X. If X is a weakly perfect GO-space and Y is a subspace of X, must Y also be weakly perfect?

evidence.quote: A space X is weakly perfect if for each closed subset C ⊆ X there is a Gδ-subset D of X with D ⊆ C = clX (D).
Question 17 ([3]). Suppose Y is a subspace of a weakly perfect GO-space X. Must Y be weakly perfect?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a topological space X weakly perfect if for every closed subset C of X there exists a G_δ subset D of X (that is, a countable intersection of open subsets of X) such that D ⊆ C and the closure of D in X equals C. A generalized ordered space (GO-space) is a triple (X, τ, <) where < is a linear order on X and τ is a Hausdorff topology on X having a base consisting of order-convex sets (sets I such that whenever a, b ∈ I and a < c < b then c ∈ I). 

Question: Suppose X is a weakly perfect GO-space and Y ⊆ X is an arbitrary subspace (endowed with the induced order and subspace topology). Must Y be weakly perfect?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether weak perfectness is hereditary among GO-spaces is listed as an open problem in the topology open-problems literature. Work by Bennett, Hosobuchi, and Lutzer constructs ZFC examples of hereditarily weakly perfect (quasi-developable) GO-spaces, but does not resolve the general hereditariness question. No source located resolves the problem in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Weakly Perfect Generalized Ordered Spaces (Bennett, Hosobuchi, Lutzer)
status_evidence.snippet: A space X is weakly perfect if each closed subset of X contains a dense Gδ-subset of X. The paper constructs ZFC quasi-developable hereditarily weakly perfect GO-spaces, indicating the hereditariness question for general weakly perfect GO-spaces remains a topic of investigation.
status_evidence.claim: The hereditariness of weak perfectness in GO-spaces is studied but not resolved in general.

status_evidence.title: Recent Developments in the Topology of Ordered Spaces (Bennett-Lutzer survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of GO-space results including weakly perfect property; no general theorem stated that subspaces of weakly perfect GO-spaces are weakly perfect.
status_evidence.claim: No published resolution found for the general subspace question.
